principle: Use the strongest label the evidence actually earns, and no stronger.

levels.name: concept-or-proposal
levels.description: Draft architecture, proposed use cases, research questions, and candidate protocol directions.

levels.name: project-authored-demonstration
levels.description: Reference demos, proof pages, example receipts, and project-maintained reproductions.

levels.name: automated-repository-verification
levels.description: CI, conformance, deterministic replay, tamper rejection, claims guards, package rehearsal, and release-coherence checks.

levels.name: independent-reproduction
levels.description: An external evaluator reproduces a defined result in an external environment.

levels.name: independent-implementation
levels.description: A separate implementation consumes public specifications, schemas, fixtures, or vectors without importing reference internals for the tested behavior.

levels.name: external-pilot-evidence
levels.description: A real external team evaluates AML in a bounded shadow, canary, or controlled pilot.

levels.name: production-deployment-evidence
levels.description: A documented external production environment uses AML for a defined scope.

levels.name: multi-party-ecosystem-evidence
levels.description: Multiple independent implementations, deployments, or evaluators produce compatible or comparable scoped results.

negative_results: FAIL and MIXED results are valid evidence and should remain citable when reproducible.
